items.headline: Upgrade three MCP reference servers to the fixed versions before reconnecting clients.
items.what_changed: The signed v2.1.0 release fixes eight vulnerabilities across Filesystem, Everything and Fetch.
items.why_it_matters: Older packages can cross configured file, browser-origin or network boundaries under documented conditions.
items.who_should_care: Builders using the official MCP reference packages in local clients, test rigs or adapted deployments.

diff.minus: Affected installs include Filesystem and Everything before 2.0.1 and Fetch through 2026.10.19.
diff.plus: Fixed packages are Filesystem 2.0.1, Everything 2.0.1 and Fetch 2026.10.24.

items.watch_out: Filesystem 2.0.1 only partly fixes the documented junction race on Windows. These servers remain educational references, not production-ready solutions.

walkthrough.use_case: Audit MCP client configurations after the v2.1.0 release and move every affected official reference server to its fixed package version.
walkthrough.steps:
Inventory every client or service configuration that launches @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem, @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything or mcp-server-fetch and record the resolved version.
Install Filesystem and Everything 2.0.1 explicitly, and install Fetch 2026.10.24. Older date-versioned npm packages may not be offered 2.0.1 automatically because package managers rank the old date numbers higher.
Restart the MCP client and confirm that its package lock or runtime log resolves the fixed version.
Re-check the Filesystem allowed directories, Everything HTTP/SSE exposure and Fetch network boundary before restoring access.
On Windows, do not allow Filesystem to use a directory writable by another user or untrusted local process; the advisory says the junction race is only partly fixed.
walkthrough.availability: Filesystem and Everything 2.0.1 are published on npm. Fetch 2026.10.24 is published on PyPI. The release is signed and dated October 25, 2026.
walkthrough.limitations: Documented upgrade walkthrough only. No package was installed, no advisory proof of concept was executed and no deployment was security-tested. The repository describes these servers as educational reference implementations.
walkthrough.evidence_label: Signed GitHub release, repository warning and linked Filesystem advisory reviewed; no live package or exploit test.

youtube_description:
The official Model Context Protocol reference servers released v2.1.0 on October 25 with fixes for eight vulnerabilities across Filesystem, Everything and Fetch. This builder briefing shows how to find affected installs, apply the exact fixed versions and review the boundaries that still matter.

- Upgrade @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem to 2.0.1.
- Upgrade @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything to 2.0.1.
- Upgrade mcp-server-fetch to 2026.10.24.
- Install the npm fixes explicitly if you still use a date-versioned package; package managers may rank the old date number above 2.0.1.
- On Windows, do not give Filesystem an allowed directory writable by another user or untrusted local process; the linked advisory says the junction race is only partly fixed.

This is a documented source review, not a live package test, exploit reproduction or security audit. The maintainers describe these servers as educational reference implementations rather than production-ready solutions.
